The rendering half of the fix already exists (supplying the type by hand in the console gives `w->length` / `w->text` with no engine change); what is absent is anything that PRODUCES a type -- set_fields_struct_raw has exactly one production caller in the tree, and the aggregate-union subphase row has advertised 'when to synthesize struct/array' with nothing behind the struct half.

root_cause: Not a defect -- a capability that has never existed. kuna's type lattice can prove what a pointer points AT but has no rule that turns a set of constant dereference offsets into a composite, so every record field read stays raw offset arithmetic.

design_corrections.precondition_pointer: The base must already be TYPE_PTR. Without it, `param` fires on fmt's get_line, whose first parameter is the real FILE * but is still typed `long`, and locks a phantom two-field layout onto it.
design_corrections.no_phi_peel: Chasing COPY/MULTIEQUAL to a root turns ls's last_component and hash_string (char * in DWARF) into two-field structures over a string; phis are not peeled and a base that reaches one declines.
design_corrections.settled_lattice: ActionInferTypes::apply returns 0 unconditionally, so has_type_recovery_started is armed after ONE of up to 7 passes. A plateau flag on the Funcdata gates the synthesizer instead. Measured with KUNA_ACTION_PROF on fmt O2: put_word runs 6 infertypes passes off / 8 on, 3 fullloops off / 4 on; main runs 9/9 in both arms because it has no accepted candidate.
design_corrections.install: Funcdata::vn_update_type_locked pairs Varnode::update_type_locked with HighVariable::type_dirty(); without the notification high_get_type returns the stale type and the printed prototype never changes. The change is signalled by bumping the action's count (Action::perform reads the return value only for res < 0). The structure is completed before its pointer is taken, for Rc identity in the merge tests.
design_corrections.widest_wins: A field wider than an access renders as a cast of the field; a field narrower than an access loses the field name entirely.
design_corrections.no_variable_length: propagate_from_pointer refuses a variable-length pointee outright and AddTreeState gives it size 0, which invalidates every TypePointerRel.
design_corrections.array_rule_gap: Howard 4.5 with exact contiguity is defeated by one untouched byte: four 1-byte stores at 0,1,3,4 gave `void gapped(struct_0 *a0)` while 0,1,2,3 correctly gave `char *`. A gap no longer breaks a uniform run below pointer width; at pointer width it still does, because a record with an untouched pointer-sized member between two observed ones is the common case (gnulib's struct hash_table is ten pointer-sized members whose readers touch different subsets of them). Cost: 3 of 304 retyped parameters.
design_corrections.array_signal_without_a_deref: `p + n` for a non-constant n is the array signal even where only a callee dereferences the result. ls O2 mpsort @0x131b0 (DWARF `void **base`) reads base[0]/base[1] itself and passes &base[n] to its callee; it was retyped and the call argument went from `&a0[a1]` to `&(&a0->field_0x0)[a1]`. It now declines and the function is byte-identical off and on.
design_corrections.dense_layout: printc.cc:1015-1033 names an in-range offset no field covers `field_0x<hex>` anyway, while compose_type_body renders the same gap as `undefined1 _pad<hex>[N]`; address arithmetic reaches those offsets without a dereference (`p + 8` prints `&p->field_0x8`). Measured: 44 `has no member named 'field_0x...'` gcc errors over 10 exported projects, fmt O2 among them. Every gap is now an `undefined1 field_0x<hex>[N]` member of alignment 1 at its own offset; filler is always an array so an array-typed member is exactly the padding.
design_corrections.c_sized: The size is the last surviving field rounded up to the widest field. A layout ending in a byte at 0x14 was 0x15 to the decompiler and 0x18 to the compiler, so `a0[1]` in the exported body was a different address (chibios chPipeReset indexes its parameter). Taking the size from the accesses, pruned ones included, also let one misaligned far access declare `undefined1 _pad10[65525]` for a 16-byte object.

interactions.libctypes: CORRECTED TWICE. The rule 'a named composite pointee always wins' protects a parameter something NAMES, and since #658 libctypes is on by default and names more than the earlier round thought. Nine of the then-301 retyped parameters were DWARF FILE * -- rpl_fseeko in all eight census binaries and fmt's fmt @0x3700 -- and the reasoning that libctypes could not see them (gnulib wrappers with no import prototype) was wrong about where the name comes from: libctypes declares `int fileno(FILE *)` and propagation carries that back into the wrapper's own parameter. Witness: `kuna decompile-all fmt --addr 0x42d0 --option structsynth param` -> `FILE *a0`; add `--option libctypes off` -> `struct_0 *a0`. get_prefix @0x2f30 and get_line @0x3420 print `FILE *a0` too. known_limits: The structure is exactly as wide as its surviving fields rounded up to their own alignment. Past that end the printer spells the address as an element of the structure array plus a byte offset: a pruned read at 0x10001 of a 16-byte layout renders as `*(unsigned int *)((long)&a0[0x1000].field_0x0 + 1)`, which compiles and computes the right address but is readable only by accident.
Offsets nobody dereferenced, and the offsets the layout prune dropped, are undefined1 filler: named and declared at their own offset, but carrying no type.

A buffer whose LAST element is written wider than the rest escapes both the uniform-run rule (the widths differ) and the prune (the wide access is past the narrow ones, not over them): ls's strmode fills a char[12] with ten 1-byte stores and one 2-byte store.
A field whose value is itself a synthesis base is not nested in this version.

struct_N names are program-wide only where one process decompiles the whole program (decompile-all, a serial decompile-project); `kuna decompile` spawns one decomp_dbg per function, and a sharded `--jobs N` run turns structsynth off in its workers, so neither has anything for the convergence sweep to do.

The layout ledger shares one record across functions by containment, so an absorbed parameter is declared with the container's whole field list -- fields its own evidence never saw. Against DWARF (main 75f832e3) pooled claimed-field precision over 169 held-out builds is 0.8908 vs 0.8902 for per-function naming, and on the second reviewer's 42 builds 0.9104 vs 0.9098, with recall higher on all eight sets; but on the 34 builds chosen last (before any result under the padding rule) it is 0.8852 vs 0.8855, and 0.9350 vs 0.9352 on 17 independently picked builds. Per binary it moves both ways: 53 of 177 builds gain, 6 lose (kmod O0/O2/O2-noinline and grep O2 under a point each, ip O0, e2fsck O0). See dedup.layout_precision.

Four measured false unifications remain out of 258 absorptions over 177 builds, all e2fsck readers with no typed pointer filled in between their own fields by a same-size layout: O0 ea_refcount_intr_next (ea_refcount answered with a dentry_info_args layout), O2-noinline ext2fs_new_dir_block (struct_ext2_filsys answered with a utf8cursor layout), and O2-noinline handle_htree / ext2fs_is_fast_symlink (ext2_inode answered with ext2_inode_large, the same record for its first 128 bytes, both added fields real). Integer words are weak evidence, and a same-size container filling holes between them is all the integer rule asks for.

Readers of different records that measured exactly the same shape share one name, as they already did on main: cp O2's struct_1 {long; long;} serves both the struct stat readers and src_to_dest_compare's Src_to_dest.

The growth bounds are not transitive, so a record can end with two names: fb claims four fields, fa two of them, fc eight including fb's four; fc is out of fa's reach and fa keeps the superseded structure it was first given (tests/cli/structsynth-sweep-mints-no-third-name.json). Which of the two fa gets depends on address order.

decompile-project --stream and the default (eager) export of the same binary report DIFFERENT numbers of records: cp O2 with `--option structsynth param` gives 31 definitions streamed against 30 eagerly (main before the ledger: 33 and 33). The convergence sweep is a property of the eager batch -- the streaming writer has already appended a body by the time a name it spells can be superseded. Each surface is self-consistent (every struct_N a body names is defined in its header). A sharded `--jobs N` run turns structsynth off in its workers, so it neither mints nor converges. The stream property the prune depends on is pinned by prune_unreferenced_synth_types over records whose `code` is None.

Speed at ledger scale: a synthetic 112 KB binary whose 1000 functions each read a different layout decompiles +12.08% against main 75f832e3 (structsynth default on; +43% before the lookup was narrowed). Real binaries measured tar O0 -0.99%, ls O2 +0.90%, rsyslogd O2 +1.02%, and ls O2 with structsynth off -0.40% (interleaved min-of-15). The residue is one scan of the held names per lookup plus the convergence sweep.

The unclaimed-bytes veto guards this pass's spelling, not the engine's ordering test: ActionMarkImplied's isPossibleAlias takes one base plus two different constants to be two objects whatever the access widths, so a load can still print after an overlapping store where the addresses are spelled that way without structsynth (raw offsets with the option off: rd_c8's `*(uint4 *)((int8)a0 + 7)` prints after `*(char *)&a0[2] = ...`). A reader the veto turns away mints its own shape beside a live container, so the record keeps two names (rsyslogd O2 syslogTime).

Records that agree on every word one of their readers measured and differ only in that reader's alignment padding keep separate names because of the padding rule: bash O0 execute_if_command/copy_if_command (if_com) vs for_com/select_com (int line at 4), the six it_init_* ITEMLIST readers vs case_com, dpkg O2-noinline pkg_queue_init (pkg_queue) vs pkg_spec (flag bytes in pkg_queue's tail padding); before the rule a reviewer measured 10 of 28 absorptions on 18 builds given a different record this way (tests/stages/structsynth-shared-layout.xml #10-#12). The cost is the reverse case: 19 absorptions onto the same record that a reader measured with a hole where its record has a member (6 of them on the first five sets: 4 into interior padding, e.g. e2fsck O2 e2fsck_get_lost_and_found, and 2 into an untyped reader's tail) now keep their own name.

A container larger than the reader's own object re-spells address arithmetic past the reader's measured end through the container's members, changing its type but not its value: cx2 (gcc -O2) rsmall returns `struct Small *p + 1`; with a larger struct Big written elsewhere the branch prints `unsigned int * sub_12b0(struct_0 *a0)` with `v1 = &a0->field_0x10;` where main prints `struct_0 * sub_12b0(struct_0 *a0)` with `v1 = &a0[1];`, and a call argument `&a0[1]` becomes `&a0->field_0x10`. The ledger sees a reader's dereferences, not the arithmetic on its base. No function in the 177 measured builds changes this way.

dedup.what: The layout ledger's second half: a measured layout is answered with an already-minted struct_N that CONTAINS it (same offset, same width, same type for every field it claims, and at least as large), instead of only with one whose layout it equals. Containment alone is not enough. A container that says strictly more must also claim at most twice as many fields and be at most four times the size, the reader must claim two fields of which one is a typed pointer, or three without one, no container member may sit in the alignment padding the reader's claims leave between two of them, and a reader with no typed pointer is answered only by a same-size structure that claims nothing past its last field: otherwise a two-word `hash_entry` reader is answered with a 200-byte `stat`, and a `struct stat *` that measured {dev, ino} is answered with the `cycle_check_state` that begins the same way, bash's `if_com` (padding at 4) is answered with `for_com` (`int line` at 4), and dpkg's `pkg_queue` with `pkg_spec` (flag bytes in `pkg_queue`'s tail padding). The other direction supersedes: a completed structure can never be widened, so the larger layout mints and the smaller is handed out again only to a layout no live structure answers for. Supersession is derived from the minted set on every lookup, for the entries that answer, not stored. And whatever the bounds say, a structure answers for a reader only if it lays exactly the reader's own members (offsets, widths, types, filler) over every byte range the reader read or wrote without claiming a field: the engine's load/store ordering test (isPossibleAlias) compares addresses without their widths, so a container that started a member inside such an access printed a 4-byte load at 7 after the byte store at 8 that overwrites it.
dedup.convergence: kuna-console/src/project.rs (converge_synthesized_structs): decompile-all runs in address order, so the smaller layout mints first; after the eager batch the driver decompiles again exactly the results that spell a superseded name as a whole identifier, and each moves to the survivor where the survivor is in its reach. One sweep, not a fixpoint, and not always one name per record: the growth bounds are not transitive (fb claims four fields, fa two of them, fc eight including fb's four; fc is out of fa's reach, so fa keeps the superseded structure it was first given). The lookup never mints a name an existing structure answers for, so the sweep mints nothing as long as a re-decided function measures what it measured the first time; the previous round minted a born-superseded third name there (tests/cli/structsynth-sweep-mints-no-third-name.json fails on it). bounds.rule: a container saying strictly more than the reader measured must claim <= 2x its claimed fields (MAX_CLAIM_GROWTH) and be <= 4x its size (MAX_SIZE_GROWTH); the reader must claim >= 2 fields of which one is a typed pointer (MIN_SHARED_CLAIMS) or >= 3 without one (MIN_UNTYPED_CLAIMS); a pointer to code, void or an undefined type is not typed; a reader whose every claim past offset 0 is such a pointer is a table and answered only by its own shape; a reader with no typed pointer is answered only by a structure of its own size that claims nothing past the reader's last field; no container answers with a member inside the alignment padding the reader's claims leave between two of them (from the end of a claim to the next claim or the next multiple of that claim's width, whichever is first); two layouts of exactly the same shape always share a name
bounds.why_claim_bound: ls O0 sub_afe2 measured two fields of an 80-byte layout and unbounded containment answered it with a sixteen-field structure only 1.5x the size
bounds.why_size_bound: ls O0 sub_12d8d takes a `struct hash_entry *` (two words) and unbounded containment declared it a 200-byte struct_5, the layout of the `struct stat *` two other functions pass; that container claims exactly 2x the fields
bounds.why_4x_not_2x: ls O2's two fileinfo comparators are one record measured at 80 and at 176 bytes; a 2x size bound refuses the witness and scores worse on the tuning set (0.8686 for size-only 2x)
bounds.why_pointer_rule: two integer words are how distinct records begin (stat {dev, ino}, cycle_check_state, Src_to_dest {ino, dev}, list nodes, timespec, hash entries) and pass both growth bounds (2 claims vs 4, 16 bytes vs 32). Over the three sets under the previous rule: two integer claims 17 same record / 44 different / 5 uncheckable; two claims with a pointer 45 / 1 / 0; three or more claims 50 / 0 / 1. The reviewer's alternative (>= 3 claims always) also refuses the ls fileinfo witness, {0: char *, 0x48: long}.
bounds.superseded_fallback: the bounds cost containment its transitivity, so when nothing live answers, the smallest superseded entry that answers is handed out rather than minting a name that entry would supersede at birth; an exact-shape entry is always the smallest answer
bounds.why_table_rule: rsyslogd O2's seven *_if_s interface records (80-136 B) are a version word then code * slots; `code *` names no record, so with the pointer rule alone all seven took statsobj_if_s's 144-byte layout and 1 of the 31 added fields was real (strgenQueryInterface 0x414e0 / statsobjQueryInterface 0x551d0)
bounds.why_integer_rule: records that begin alike part ways after the last field a reader touched: ip's netlink readers measure the same nlmsghdr words ahead of different payloads (13 absorptions on heldout3/4 added 34 fields, 0 real); dpkg pkg_queue (24 B) was answered with a 40-byte command layout (0/3 real). Cost: openssh sshbuf readers measuring 64 of 72 bytes keep their own name
bounds.why_padding_rule: records part ways in their first words as well as after their last: a reviewer's 18 builds (bash O0, dpkg O2-noinline, ...) gave 10 of 28 absorptions a different record, all a same-size container with a member where the reader has padding: bash O0 execute_if_command/copy_if_command (if_com {0: uint, 8, 0x10, 0x18}) and copy_while_command answered with for_com (int line at 4); six it_init_* ITEMLIST readers ({0: uint, 0x10: long *}) answered with case_com; dpkg O2-noinline pkg_queue_init (pkg_queue, 24 B) answered with pkg_spec (flag bytes at 0x14/0x15, pkg_queue's tail padding). With the rule: 0 of 13 on those builds, and over all 177 builds it removes 30 of the previous revision's absorptions (11 different record, 19 same record) and adds none. A hole wider than its padding may still be filled, and a typed reader may still take tail members (fmt put_word {0: char *, 8: int} of WORD, whose int space is at 0xc)

unclaimed_bytes.rule: ledger.rs keeps_unclaimed: for every (offset, width) the prune dropped from the reader's evidence, the candidate structure's members overlapping those bytes must equal the reader's own members there (offset, size, claimed field key or filler); checked only for candidates that already answer by containment and the bounds, and only when the reader has an unclaimed access
unclaimed_bytes.why: ActionMarkImplied::checkImpliedCover lets a LOAD cross a STORE unless isPossibleAlias says the addresses may alias, and isPossibleAlias answers 'no' for one base plus two different constants whatever the access widths. The reader's own layout spells an unclaimed access through filler (&a0->field_0x4[3]), which the test cannot separate from a field, so it stays explicit; a container member starting inside the access made it a direct field address (&a0->field_0x7) and the load printed after an overlapping byte store.
unclaimed_bytes.counterexample: gcc -O2 stripped: full(p,v,s) writes c7..c10, i0, l10, s, l20; rd_c8(p,s,w) { memcpy(&v,&p->c7,4); p->c8=w>>3; ... return v*3u; }. Previous revision: rd_c8 answered with full's struct, `return *(uint4 *)&a0->field_0x7 * 3` after `a0->field_0x8 = ...`; the printed body returned 0xd5c06096 where the original returns 0xd5c0ab96 (stores at 9 and 10 the same; a store at 7 is safe). Shipped: each reader keeps its own shape and `v1 = *(uint4 *)&a0->field_0x4[3];` stays first, as on main.
unclaimed_bytes.measured: all 101 builds of the five sets, main f1ec42a7 vs this revision vs the previous one: exactly one parameter changes, rsyslogd O2 timeConvertToUTC's struct syslogTime * (a 4-byte store at 7 answered with a same-size layout declaring bytes 7..10); it returns to its own 10-claim shape and main's body, losing 4 true fields (heldout3 0.8409 -> 0.8407; pooled held-out stays 0.8747). The whole-corpus sweep's one non-rename hunk (that store split into four byte stores) is gone.
unclaimed_bytes.engine_defect_not_fixed_here: isPossibleAlias ignores access widths on raw offsets too: with structsynth off, rd_c8 prints `*(uint4 *)((int8)a0 + 7)` after `*(char *)&a0[2] = (char)(a2 >> 3)`. That is a separate strict engine fix.

dedup.container_larger_than_reader: a container larger than the reader's own object re-spells address arithmetic past the reader's measured end through the container's members: reviewer cx2 (gcc -O2) rsmall(struct Small {char *; long;} *p) returns p + 1, and with struct Big {char *; long; int; int; long;} written elsewhere the branch prints `unsigned int * sub_12b0(struct_0 *a0)` ... `v1 = &a0->field_0x10;` where main prints `struct_0 * sub_12b0(struct_0 *a0)` ... `v1 = &a0[1];` (rsmall_arg's call argument `&a0[1]` likewise becomes `&a0->field_0x10`). Same address and value, different type. The ledger sees a reader's dereferences, not the arithmetic on its base. No function in the 177 builds changes this way (the one non-rename code change is ip O0 ll_remember_index)
